pr_title: systemd-sleep: always attempt hibernation if configured
pr_body:
When calculation of swap file offset is unsupported, rely on the `/sys/power/resume` & `/sys/power/resume_offset` values rather than requiring a matching swap entry to be identified.

Refactor to use `dev_t` for comparison of `resume=` device instead of `string`.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/14249

@poettering migrating the resume device comparison from `string` to `dev_t` re-exposed the fact that Btrfs will not return the correct `dev_t` from `stat`. in the end, I think the best course of action is to give Btrfs users the ability to override `find_hibernate_location` - if they have `/sys/power/resume` and `/sys/power/resume_offset` configured correctly, hibernation should work (unless there isn't enough space). 

I simplified the change to:

1. User `dev_t` over `string` for `resume=` device.
2. Added ability to override the `find_hibernate_location` logic 
3. Improved or added additional logging and comments.

I'm not sure that re-using the `SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK` environment variable is the best idea for overriding the `find_hibernate_location` logic. On the one hand it's current use implies the user has their swaps configured correctly and they know what they're doing so we don't need to try and discover anything but it's not explicitly clear. It might make more sense to introduce a new variable that is specific to Btrfs like `SYSTEMD_HIBERNATE_WITH_BTRFS_SWAPFILE=1` or maybe something less specific to Btrfs but more specific to the objective like `SYSTEMD_HIBERNATE_DISABLE_SWAP_DISCOVERY=1`.

If this approach seems reasonable, I'll go ahead and squash the commits and make any remaining changes you'd suggest.

Thanks as  always for the help!

issue_context.title: Systemd 244 Hibernation failed due to sys/power/resume and /sys/power/resume_offset has no matching entry in /proc/swaps
issue_context.body:
`systemctl hibernate` was working in 243 but failed in 244 with error:

```
Dec 04 17:21:09 liberty-pc systemd-logind[551]: /sys/power/resume and /sys/power/resume_offset has no matching entry in /proc/swaps; Hibernation will fail: resume=259:7, resume_offset=52582877
```

The resume_offset in kernel parameter is correctly set and hibernation works in version 243.

```
% cat /proc/swaps 
Filename				Type		Size	Used	Priority
/swapfile                               file		20971516	0	-2

% cat /proc/cmdline 
initrd=\intel-ucode.img initrd=\initramfs-linux.img root=PARTUUID=fd43dfa1-32dd-444e-a802-b1c696bd57be rootflags=subvol=/root resume=PARTUUID=fd43dfa1-32dd-444e-a802-b1c696bd57be resume_offset=52582877 zswap.enabled=1 zswap.compressor=zstd zswap.max_pool_percent=20 zswap.zpool=z3fold rw
```

**Used distribution**
 > Arch linux

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > systemctl hbiernate should succeed

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > systemctl hibernate failed

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
* Use BTRFS swap file 
* Follow instruction https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/Power_management/Suspend_and_hibernate#Hibernation_into_swap_file_on_Btrfs to create swapfile
* Verified swap file works and has enough space.  
* Verified Hibernation works by running `echo disk > /sys/power/state`
* Run `systemctl hibernate`
* `systemctl hibernate` failed saying not enough space
* `journalctl -ae` shows error Hibernation failed due to sys/power/resume and /sys/power/resume_offset has no matching entry in /proc/swaps
comments: @zachsmith ?

I'm affected as well by this since the upgrade to systemd 244. 
Arch Linux

Looking at the relevant code in [`sleep-config.c`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/src/shared/sleep-config.c), it appears as if the following happens:

- [`calculate_swap_file_offset`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L216) does not support calculating the file offset on Btrfs file systems, returning an offset of 0 instead: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L237-L238
- [`location_is_resume_device`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L283) compares the file offset calculated by `calculate_swap_file_offset` (i.e. 0 on Btrfs) with the `resume_offset` kernel command line parameter, which fails: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L288
- As a result, the [loop](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L321-L391) in [`find_hibernate_location`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L300) never finds the correct swap entry, using the ["highest priority swap with most remaining space"](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L366) instead: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L387-L389
- Finally, `location_is_resume_device` is used on the selected swap entry, which fails again (even if it is indeed the correct entry) and produces the warning mentioned in the bug report: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/9142bbd19c932e9fd248f613abfc39fad66e9f23/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L396-L398

An (untested) quick fix would be to use
```c
return streq(sys_resume, location->resume) && ((location->resume_offset == 0) || (sys_offset == location->resume_offset));
```
in `location_is_resume_device` so that the comparison can succeed on Btrfs filesystems. This means if the device given by the `resume` kernel command line argument has a Btrfs file system, `find_hibernate_location` will use the first swap file on the device listed in `/proc/swaps`.

The only situation where I can see this failing is when there are multiple swap files on a single Btrfs device and the one specified by `resume_offset` is not the first one listed in `/proc/swaps`. However in this case we cannot do any better at the moment anyway since calculating the file offset for Btrfs to find the correct file is not implemented. On the other hand, the most common case of at most one Btrfs swap file is covered.
Thanks for reporting this and sorry for the headache. I'll get a fix up for this soon.

Apparantly on Btrfs even the [device ID from `fstat` does not match the actual device ID](https://www.mail-archive.com/linux-btrfs@vger.kernel.org/msg57667.html), so the quick fix above should read
```c
return location->resume_offset == 0 || (streq(sys_resume, location->resume) && sys_offset == location->resume_offset);
```
instead (i.e. use the swap file on any Btrfs file system that is listed first in `/proc/swaps`). I was able to successfully test this workaround on a system with a single swap file on a (LUKS-encrypted) Btrfs file system.

I posted a fix here: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/14270.

As a result, I made a small change that will intentionally cause hibernation to fail in some cases so you will need to set `SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK=1` in your `systemd-logind.service` `[Service]` section.

Unfortunately the latest patch does not work. Hibernation failed, and  `journalctl` does not give error log anymore also.
```
% systemctl hibernate
Failed to hibernate system via logind: Not enough swap space for hibernation

% SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK=1 systemctl hibernate
Failed to hibernate system via logind: Not enough swap space for hibernation
```

Sorry I wasn't clearer about that before. You'll need to set `SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK=1` in the `[Service]` section of the `systemd-logind.service`. You should be able to do that with `systemctl edit systemd-logind.service`

```
[Service]
Environment=SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK=1
...
```

I believe you'll need to reboot after making that change.

The message that you're seeing now is coming from `logind` and hibernation isn't being attempted because systemd can't determine if there is enough space. When using swap files on Btrfs, the previous code would try to check for space and would pass in most cases but was not necessarily checking the correct swap file. This was one of the edge cases I discovered today. The swap file offset is needed to match the `resume=` and `resume_offset=` values with a `/proc/swaps` entry and that is needed to check for enough space. Because we can't detect the correct offset on Btrfs for the swapfile we can't correctly find the swap entry and we can't check the space. 

There has been the ability to bypass this check for some time so you'll need to use that here.

You should also be able to see a debug message in the log that reads something like:

`Unable to determine available swap space for resume=8:17, resume_offset=487840; set SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK=1 to override this check.`

Hibernation works with SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK in /etc/systemd/system/systemd-logind.service.d/override.conf
Probably I don't understand swap space calculation correctly. I thought it is just swap file size should be larger than image size.
Also does that mean SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK for all cases that btrfs swap file is used?

```
% cat /sys/power/image_size 
13233156096

% ls -l swapfile
-rw------- 1 root root 21474836480 Sep 10 21:42 swapfile
```

@helloworld1 to try and answer your question, in order to correctly detect the remaining swap space, we need to know how much space is already in use. We do that by parsing `/proc/swaps` and attempting to match a swap entry with `resume=` and `resume_offset=` values to make checking for space on the right file. In order to match the swap file entry in `/proc/swaps` we need to calculate the offset...which we don't have support for right now when using Btrfs. So we can't match the entries in `/proc/swaps` with `resume` and `resume_offset` and can't find the space in use.

Because we can't correctly identify the swap file, we can't correctly see how much space is in use so even if we know the size of the image and the size of the file, we won't know if it'll fit.

https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/src/shared/sleep-config.c#L436

In the past we were just returning the first swap in the list and the space calculation would run and if you only had one swap entry that was your swap file configured for `resume` and resume_offset`, it would pass...but that was just coincidence.

And yes, `SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK` will apply in all cases - regardless of file system. It's not specific to Btrfs.
Thanks for the explanation. Is the problem specific to BTRFS or all swap files? If it applies to all sway files, should we make space check bypass default for all swap files?

@helloworld1 @diabonas I've updated the patch a bit to focus more on giving Btrfs swapfile users a way to disable the swap discovery logic. I think this is the best course of action for a few reasons:  if you are intending to use a swapfile on Btrfs you must have your system configured correctly (`/sys/power/{resume, resume_offset}` must be set with correct device id and offset which must be calculated) and if the system is not configured correctly, systemd will not be able to help discover the swap file for you by parsing `/proc/swaps`.

The current patch will require that you add:
```
[Service]
Environment=SYSTEMD_BYPASS_HIBERNATION_MEMORY_CHECK=1
```

to `systemd-logind` (logind checks for memory) and `systemd-hibernate` (attempts discovery to match swap files with configured devices) services.

This is still not OK. We *can* distinguish the cases where:
- there is no swap in /proc/swaps
- there is a device in /proc/swaps but a different device is configured in /sys/power/resume
- /sys/power/resume is populated and there's a matching device in /proc/swaps but we cannot verify the offset.

With your patch, after `swapoff -a` I get:
```
/sys/power/resume appears to be configured but a matching swap in /proc/swaps could not be identified; hibernation may fail
Unable to determine remaining swap space; hibernation may fail
Hibernation configured and possible: yes
```
But hibernation will surely fail, so saying that it "might fail" is wrong.
